rules.title: Berkeley Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions to refuse, terminate, or charge more. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history, they must give written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de Berkeley no pueden preguntar sobre los antecedentes penales ni usarlos en anuncios, solicitudes, selección de inquilinos o decisiones de rechazar, terminar o cobrar más. Si el arrendador toma una acción basada en antecedentes penales, debe dar aviso por escrito y la oportunidad de responder.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, including advertising, applications, tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner resides; owner move-back units under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages (actual or three times one month's rent), punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.caveat: Passed April 14, 2020; effective date not stated in document. Secondary page summarizing ordinance.
